page: Microsoft Azure E2d_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance deployed on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is driven by a 2.6 GHz Intel Xeon 8272CL processor based on the x86_64 architecture, providing 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 1 physical core with 2 threads. Cache hierarchy includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 35 MB of L3 cache. It features support for extended instructions such as AVX-512F, AVX-512 VNNI, AES, and FMA. Hardware resources include 16.0 GB of memory, yielding 8.0 GB per vCPU, along with 81 GB of integrated local SSD storage. No discrete GPU acceleration is included, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are attached.

Performance evaluations indicate distinct profiles between single-threaded and parallel compute routines. Single-core evaluations, including Geekbench at 1264.0 and gzip compression at 24.02 GB/sec, demonstrate moderate performance. In contrast, multi-threaded CPU tests fall into lower percentiles due to the two-vCPU hardware ceiling, yielding 1840.88 in multi-core stress-ng and 1530.0 in multi-core Geekbench. Uncached memory read bandwidth measures 14.22 GB/sec, while write bandwidth reaches 11.16 GB/sec. Application-level throughput shows Redis processing 1.77 million SET operations per second and static web serving achieving 2.06 GB/sec. Small 135M model prompt processing reaches 111.83 tokens per second with generation at 36.61 tokens per second.

From a cost and resource perspective, the instance is engineered for architectures requiring elevated memory-to-core ratios rather than heavy parallel calculation. The inclusion of bundled 81 GB local SSD storage provides low-latency ephemeral caching and scratch space without relying solely on remote volumes. Due to the two-vCPU allocation, computational bottlenecks will arise under heavy processing or concurrent compilation workloads. The Azure E2d_v4 is suitable for small in-memory caching nodes, low-throughput relational database deployments, staging environments, and intermediate batch processing tasks with moderate memory requirements.
description: Microsoft Azure E2d_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor running at 2.6 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Managed via Microsoft Hyper-V, the system provides 2 dedicated vCPUs across 1 physical core, equipped with 35 MB of L3 cache, AVX-512 support, and 16.0 GB of RAM, establishing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. It also integrates 81 GB of local SSD temporary storage with zero discrete GPU hardware. Single-core responsiveness and compression metrics demonstrate moderate throughput, while multi-threaded benchmarks reflect the constraints of its two-thread limit. Cost efficiency is centered on memory allocation rather than pure raw compute capability. The server is well positioned for small relational databases, entry-level in-memory cache services like Redis, local caching deployments, and small-scale backend tasks prioritizing RAM capacity over multi-core parallel execution.
